text: The latest update did not improve battery life at all.
rationale: Tests whether the model picks up the negation cue or just the trigger word 'improve'

text: This app is no longer reliable on my phone.
rationale: Strong positive cue 'reliable' negated by 'no longer'; tests cue-vs-context handling

text: The team won the championship final last weekend.
rationale: Sports content unrelated to app-review training; tests domain-shift robustness

text: I do not love the new layout anymore.
rationale: Uses negation before a strong positive cue 'love' to test whether the model follows the negation.

text: The update is not helpful and made the app harder to use.
rationale: Uses 'not helpful' to test whether the model catches the negative meaning instead of the positive cue.

text: I cannot say this app is bad after the latest fix.
rationale: Uses negation cue 'bad' to test whether the model can flip polarity.

text: The app is not perfect but it works well for my daily tasks.
rationale: Uses 'not perfect' with an overall positive meaning to test mixed negation handling.

text: I do not have any serious complaints about this version.
rationale: Uses negation around 'complaints' to test if the model mistakes the negative word for negative sentiment.

text: The app looks beautiful but crashes every time I open it.
rationale: Contains positive cue 'beautiful' but the real sentiment is negative because the app crashes.

text: Great design, terrible performance.
rationale: Uses strong positive cue 'great' followed by a stronger negative complaint.

text: I loved the old version, but this update ruined it.
rationale: Contains positive cue 'loved' while the sentence is negative about the current app.

text: The support team is friendly, but they never solve the issue.
rationale: Contains positive cue 'friendly' but the unresolved issue makes the review negative.

text: The app is fast, but the payment fails every time.
rationale: Contains positive cue 'fast' while the main functional complaint is negative.

text: This is reliable only when I do not actually need it.
rationale: Uses positive cue 'reliable' in a sarcastic negative context.

text: The recipe needs more salt and ten minutes in the oven.
rationale: Recipe content is outside app reviews and should not imply app sentiment.

text: The stock market closed higher after strong technology earnings.
rationale: News-style sentence tests whether business words trigger sentiment labels.

text: The player scored twice before halftime.
rationale: Sports sentence is unrelated to app quality and should be neutral.

text: Heavy rain is expected across the northern region tomorrow.
rationale: Weather sentence tests domain shift away from app-review language.

text: The museum opened a new exhibition about ancient trade routes.
rationale: Cultural news sentence is outside app-review sentiment.

text: The laptop has sixteen gigabytes of memory and a silver keyboard.
rationale: Product specification sentence should be neutral rather than positive or negative.

text: Works great.
rationale: Very short review tests whether the model can classify minimal positive text.

text: Crashes constantly.
rationale: Very short review tests whether the model can classify minimal negative text.

text: It is okay.
rationale: Very short review tests whether the model can handle weak neutral sentiment.

text: I installed the app after the update and at first it opened normally, but after I changed the settings, added my account, enabled notifications, and tried to use the main feature, it became slower, froze twice, and made the whole experience frustrating.
rationale: Long sentence with several details tests whether the model keeps track of the main negative conclusion.

text: I used the app for a full week, and although there were a few small delays when switching screens, the reminders worked, the interface was clear, and it helped me finish my tasks more consistently.
rationale: Long mixed sentence tests whether the model captures the overall positive conclusion.

text: The app has a menu, a profile page, notification settings, and a search button.
rationale: Longer descriptive sentence lists features without clear sentiment.

text: Amazing, another crash right when I needed the app most.
rationale: Surface word 'Amazing' is positive but the intended meaning is negative sarcasm.

text: Perfect, now I get to restart the app every five minutes.
rationale: Positive cue 'Perfect' is used sarcastically with a negative complaint.

text: Great, the app deleted my progress again.
rationale: Positive cue 'Great' is sarcastic because the app caused data loss.

text: I just love waiting forever for a simple page to load.
rationale: Positive phrase 'love' is sarcastic because the waiting complaint is negative.

text: Wonderful, now the app freezes every time I try to check my account.
rationale: Positive cue 'Wonderful' is used sarcastically because the app freezing is a negative experience.

text: Lovely, another update that removed the only feature I actually used.
rationale: Positive cue 'Lovely' is sarcastic because the update removed an important feature.
